# GenLayer Research

> A visual guide to GenLayer's research on automating ambiguous decisions in adversarial environments: sampled panels of AI judges, exact reproducibility guarantees, cost-aware evaluation, appeal incentives, and machine-checked verification of the Optimistic Democracy protocol.

The guide is a single page available in five languages; the papers are PDFs.

## Guide

- [Research guide (English)](https://genlayerlabs.github.io/research/)
- [Guía en español](https://genlayerlabs.github.io/research/es/)
- [한국어 안내서](https://genlayerlabs.github.io/research/ko/)
- [简体中文指南](https://genlayerlabs.github.io/research/zh/)
- [Руководство на русском](https://genlayerlabs.github.io/research/ru/)

## Papers

- [GenLayer Whitepaper v2](https://genlayerlabs.github.io/research/papers/genlayer-whitepaper-v2.pdf): the system paper: execution environment, Optimistic Democracy consensus, protocol economics
- [Aggregate Disambiguation Systems](https://genlayerlabs.github.io/research/papers/part-1-aggregate-disambiguation-systems.pdf): exact finite-panel reproducibility — how often a sampled panel of AI judges matches its declared pool, with and without corruption
- [Adaptive Economic Aggregate Disambiguation](https://genlayerlabs.github.io/research/papers/part-2-adaptive-economic-disambiguation.pdf): cost-aware evaluation policies that spend more judgment only where decisions are close
- [Layered Formal Verification of the Optimistic Democracy Protocol](https://genlayerlabs.github.io/research/papers/part-3-layered-formal-verification.pdf): a machine-checked TLA+ model chain from canonical state graph to committed Solidity
- [Multi-Agent Appeal Games in Aggregate Disambiguation Systems](https://genlayerlabs.github.io/research/papers/part-4-multi-agent-appeal-games.pdf): when private incentives produce the appeals the protocol needs — and when they stay unfiled or duplicated
